Reddit is looking for a Group Product Manager to lead the product management of our Finance SaaS portfolio, our systems that run treasury, planning, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, quote-to-cash, payroll, and equity.

This is a player-coach role: you'll coach and manage a small team of SaaS product managers who each own a domain of Finance's application stack, while personally owning your own set of applications as a player.

This role serves as the orchestration layer for Finance and AI Transformation, requiring you to advise senior executives, influence strategic direction, and navigate complex matrixed environments to translate high-level strategy into measurable business outcomes.
You set the product vision and roadmap across the Finance SaaS landscape, decide what gets built and bought, drive adoption, and own the vendor relationships that underpin the stack. You partner closely with the Enterprise Architecture & Engineering team. They own how systems are built and integrated; you own what we build, why, and when.
You will be at the forefront of our AI-first finance strategy, championing the next generation of intelligent automation to redefine efficiency and scalability across our global operations. If you're energized by translating complex finance processes into clean, well-run systems, thrive at the seam between business and technology, and want to both lead a team and stay close to the product yourself, this role is for you.

Product Strategy & Portfolio Ownership
Own the end-to-end product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for Reddit's Finance SaaS portfolio across P2P, R2R, QTC, payroll & equity, and treasury/investments/EPM.
As the lead for Finance & AI Transformation, you are the catalyst for shifting Reddit’s finance teams from manual processes to AI-enabled workflows. This includes championing a “finance engineer” mindset, proactively identifying AI use cases for close automation and anomaly detection, and fostering a culture where data-driven innovation is embedded in our operating model.
Translate Finance's priorities (e.g., close acceleration, scalability, public-company rigor, M&A) into a sequenced, defensible roadmap.
Lead build-vs-buy and vendor selection decisions; serve as the product voice in Finance technology investments alongside the Enterprise Architect.
Define and enforce a consistent product operating model across the team: intake, prioritization, release management, change management, and adoption measurement.
Identify opportunities to improve Finance processes through AI-enabled workflows, reconciliations, anomaly detection, approval copilots, and close automation.
Drive roadmap prioritization using measurable outcomes such as close cycle reduction, automation rates, SOX compliance effectiveness, and Finance productivity improvements.
Establish a single, transparent demand pipeline so Finance stakeholders can see what's planned, in flight, and shipped.
Assess the end-to-end finance processes to identify manual workflows, process gaps, control weaknesses, data quality issues, and opportunities to improve and enable AI-powered solutions..
Create a cross-functional decision framework for Finance capabilities, including clear ownership, intake, prioritization, readiness criteria, and business sign-off.
Identify, design, and launch new features and system capabilities that enhance user efficiency while driving incremental value for the business.
Partner with finance leadership to enable AI use across teams, fundamentally shifting the organization toward a "finance engineer" mindset where finance teams are empowered to build, automate, and innovate within our systems.
Drive end-to-end finance transformation initiatives across Quote-to-Cash (QTC), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Record-to-Report (R2R), and Hire-to-Retire (H2R), ensuring alignment between process improvements and long-term scalability.
Strategic Orchestration & Influence
Advise senior Finance and Tech leadership on roadmap trade-offs, balancing speed, risk, and long-term impact.
Navigate organizational dynamics to secure alignment across Finance, Tech, and Business partners.
Promote harmony between internal teams and external integration partners by resolving bottlenecks and managing cross-functional dependencies.
Lead a rigorous diligence program to evaluate and optimize system performance, workflows, and adoption metrics to strengthen operational quality.
Team Leadership
Directly manage a team of SaaS product managers, each owning a Finance domain (P2P & R2R, QTC, Payroll & Equity).
Set clear direction and priorities for each domain, and create space for deep, high-quality product work.
Develop your team's craft through roadmap review, stakeholder coaching, and regular 1:1s focused on growth.
Serve as an escalation point and thought partner when your PMs hit ambiguity, contention over priorities, or cross-functional friction.
Build the bench: define the team's coverage model, identify gaps, and grow the function as Finance scales.

Maintain direct ownership over a specific set of applications, leading their product roadmaps and managing key stakeholder relationships.
This isn't a purely managerial role: you'll run intake, prioritize enhancements, manage releases, and partner directly with Finance and the Eng team to deliver in your own portfolio.
Stay close enough to the work to credibly coach your team and make sharp product tradeoffs.
Vendor and Demand Management
Own Finance SaaS vendor relationships at the portfolio level: renewals, SLAs, roadmap influence, escalations, and spend rationalization.
Bring a demand-management mindset to intake; help Finance stakeholders articulate needs, size effort, and sequence work effectively rather than absorbing every request.
Partner with Procurement and Finance leadership on tooling spend, contract timing, and consolidation opportunities.
Maintain a clear view of total cost of ownership and license utilization across the stack.
Stakeholder Partnership
Act as the primary product liaison for Finance leadership, translating business requirements into roadmap decisions and communicating tradeoffs clearly.
Partner with FP&A, Technical Accounting, Revenue, Treasury, Payroll, and Finance Operations to understand pain points and proactively surface system improvements.
Work hand-in-glove with the Enterprise Architect and Engineering team to land integrations, data quality, and technical delivery against the product roadmap.
Support M&A activity (e.g., systems due diligence, gap analysis, integration sequencing, and adoption planning for acquired entities).

Greenlight is a family technology company on a mission to help families raise financially smart kids and navigate life together. Its suite of products — including the Greenlight app, debit card, Safe Family GPS trackers, and Family Hub — brings together financial tools, safety features, and everyday family management in one connected experience.

Designed for busy families who want convenience without compromise, Greenlight continues to innovate alongside the evolving needs of modern life. Today, more than 6.5 million family members trust Greenlight to stay in sync.
At Greenlight , we're here to make the day-to-day easier and futures brighter, so families can spend less time managing life, and more time living it. That's why we get out of bed every morning.
Registration is the most critical growth lever Greenlight has - it’s where millions of families decide to take the leap.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager, Growth to own and optimize this journey end-to-end: driving incremental registrations, improving conversion across every step of the funnel, and shipping experiments fast enough to compound learning into measurable growth.

This is a high-visibility, high-urgency role sitting at the center of Greenlight ’s Growth team. You’ll work cross-functionally with Marketing, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Payments, Partnerships, Legal, Risk and Compliance and you’ll have direct line-of-sight to executive leadership.

The right person moves fast, thinks in experiments, and treats every data point as a signal to act on. This role reports to the Senior Director of Product and sits within the Product Led Growth team.

You will be embedded in a dedicated cross-functional pod with Engineering and Design, with close partnerships across Marketing, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Payments, Partnerships, Legal, Risk and Compliance. Your day-to-day:
Own the end-to-end registration funnel: from the moment a visitor lands to the moment they become an active Greenlight family.
Identify and eliminate friction at every step: form design, identity verification, plan selection, payment, and onboarding handoffs.
Build and maintain a prioritized experiment backlog informed by funnel analytics, user research, and competitive teardowns.
Target 6+ experiments per month, designing tests that are statistically sound, fast to ship, and easy to learn from.
Define and own the primary success metric: reg conversion rate (reg complete / sessions) across the full funnel, with reg start as a leading indicator.
Tier experiment surfaces by traffic volume prioritizing high-volume flows where you can call wins on statistical significance in reg complete.
Optimize for quality of registrations, not just volume - track downstream signals including engagement and early retention.
Run A/B and multivariate tests across registration screens, pricing displays, plan framing, onboarding steps, and upsell surfaces.
Develop strategic growth initiatives beyond incremental optimization
Work closely with Marketing to ensure continuity between ad creative and landing/registration experience: reducing intent-to-action drop-off.
Partner with the Upgrades PM to create a coherent journey from acquisition through premium conversion.
Bring customer psychology to your decision-making: understand what motivates parents to start, what creates hesitation, and how to design flows that build confidence at each step.
Write sharp, actionable product requirements that unblock engineering rather than constrain it.
Work in an agile environment with a dedicated pod: maintaining high execution velocity while managing Legal and Compliance review in a regulated industry.
Communicate experiment results, product bets, and roadmap priorities clearly and regularly to senior leadership.
Iterate quickly: use post-launch data to inform the next experiment before the current one is cold.

s.h: What you’ll bring to the team
s.t:
6+ years of product management experience, with a focus on conversion funnel optimization, growth, or registration/onboarding in a consumer-facing product.
A proven experimentation track record - you’ve run high-velocity experiment programs (4+/month) and know how to design, call, and sequence tests for maximum learning.
Deep comfort with funnel analytics: you should be ready to pull your own data, know your way around SQL or BI tools (Mixpanel, Amplitude, Looker), and can distinguish signal from noise.
Strong cross-functional instincts - you’ve navigated complex stakeholder environments including Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Payments, and know how to move fast within constraints.
Executive presence: you communicate up and across clearly, adapt your message to your audience, and don’t wait to be asked for updates.
Ownership mentality - you proactively identify gaps, propose solutions, and follow through. You don’t need a playbook to get started.
Urgency and scrappiness: experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments where speed matters and you figure things out yourself.
Customer psychology instincts - you think about why users behave the way they do, not just what they do.

Experience with mobile or app-based registration and onboarding flows.
Familiarity with KYC, identity verification, or regulated financial product flows.
Experience working in a subscription or freemium model with a focus on trial-to-paid conversion.

Invicti is looking for a Principal Technical Product Manager to own our Code & Developer Security product area - spanning SAST, SCA, IaC, Container Security, and Secrets Detection. This is a high-ownership, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build products that security and engineering teams actually trust: better signal, less noise, faster fixes. These products will be a significant part of the Invicti AppSec Platform.

AI is changing how software gets written, and it's changing this product area faster than almost any other. Development teams using AI coding assistants are shipping more code, faster, with less visibility into what's in it.

That means larger attack surfaces, more opaque dependency chains, more auto-generated IaC, and secrets in places no one reviewed. The tools that win in this environment won't just scan more, they'll surface what actually matters, with enough context that a developer can act on it without filing a ticket.
At the same time, Invicti 's portfolio is expanding. Our recently delivered ASPM platform creates a correlation layer above individual scan results. Octo, our agentic offensive security capability, is beginning to close the loop between static findings and validated exploitability. The Code Security product area sits at the foundation of this stack, and this PM will shape how those connections get built.

Full product ownership for the Code Security product area, SAST, SCA, IaC, Container Security, and Secrets Detection, across the Invicti and Acunetix product lines
Roadmap definition and prioritization grounded in customer evidence, market data, and portfolio strategy.
A point of view on how AI-assisted development changes the threat model, and how our scanning, triage, and remediation capabilities need to evolve in response
Positioning in a highly competitive market that includes incumbents and a growing set of AI-native entrants rethinking what static analysis can do

5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years in a technical PM role at a security, developer tools, or infrastructure company desired
Familiarity with at least two of the core domains: SAST, SCA, IaC security, container security, or secrets management
A perspective on how AI-assisted development changes the security problem
Strong written communication
Experience working in a multi-product environment where roadmap decisions require cross-portfolio thinking
The ability to move with conviction under ambiguity, and the seniority to bring others along through influence
Strong ability to use current AI tools to improve the product development lifecycle.

Prior experience at a SAST, SCA, or software supply chain security vendor
Exposure to ASPM platforms or consolidated security findings workflows
Background shipping developer-facing products or integrations into CI/CD pipelines

Invicti Security helps more than 4,000 organizations worldwide secure web applications and APIs with the industry’s most accurate application security platform, powered by 20 years of technology leadership in DAST. Combining proof-based testing, runtime intelligence, and continuous innovation, Invicti enables AppSec teams to identify real risk, reduce alert noise, and ship secure software faster.
Invicti 's proof-based philosophy, validate what's actually exploitable before surfacing it, sets a high bar for signal quality. Code Security is where that philosophy needs to extend upstream, into a world where AI is generating more code than any team can manually review. The PM who defines that product direction, at this moment, is doing genuinely consequential work.

Who We Are
Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.
We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.
You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

This position sits on the Business Systems Product team in the CIO organization.
Verkada sells through partners. Two products carry that motion: the Verkada Store (vStore) , where partners quote, price, and order, and the Partner Portal , where partners run their Verkada business — registering deals, tracking orders and renewals, pulling pricebooks and inventory, requesting marketing funds, and reaching the training and enablement they need to sell. You own both. One partner experience, two surfaces.
Verkada's ambition is to be the easiest company in the industry to do business with, and the Store and the Portal are where that promise is either kept or broken. Team
Join the FinOps Platform Engineering organization within Global Cloud Services (GCS), the team that builds ServiceNow’s internal FinOps Control Tower for cloud cost governance, financial accountability, and unit economics across our multi-cloud estate (AWS, Azure, and GCP).

Our organization is structured around three core teams: a Data Engineering and Data Lake team that builds the ELT pipelines landing data into our Iceberg lakehouse and owns data governance; a Platform Services team that operates our open-source platform stack (Trino, Lightdash, Coder, Jupyter, Redash, Hive Metastore/Nessie); and an Analytics Engineering team that builds the dbt data models and supports analysts creating dashboards and data apps.
This role supports the first two of those teams. You will be the product voice for the data engineering and platform services workstreams, working as a collaborative peer alongside the engineering leaders who own execution.
Role
As Senior Staff Technical Product Owner for FinOps Data Platform & Engineering, you own the product direction for both the data lake and ELT pipeline capabilities and the platform services that data engineers and analysts build on every day. You are the connective tissue between what the organization needs from its data foundation and what the engineering teams build.
This is a hands-on technical product role embedded in engineering. You will own the backlogs for two teams, translate requirements from internal users and FinOps stakeholders into concrete specifications, sequence the roadmap, and drive adoption. You will not manage people directly. You lead through influence, deep technical judgment, and close partnership with the engineering managers and senior engineers who own delivery.
Your stakeholders span both directions. Inward, you serve the data engineers, platform engineers, and analytics engineers who use the pipelines and platforms daily. Outward, you serve the FinOps practitioners, finance leaders, and capacity planners who depend on data landing reliably and platforms being available when they need them.
A defining part of the mandate is developer experience. The people building on this platform (data engineers using Coder workspaces, writing dbt models, running notebooks, querying Trino) are your users too. You will advocate for improvements to their workflows and partner with the platform services manager to make those improvements real.
You will also translate data governance requirements from compliance, security, and enterprise governance teams into actionable engineering work. You will not define governance policy, but you will ensure the platform and pipelines implement it correctly and completely.
The broader organization is migrating off Cloudera onto the modern lakehouse. You will partner closely with the Data Engineering team on this effort, jointly owning the sequencing of workload migration, defining readiness criteria for each wave, and coordinating stakeholder communication. The Principal Engineer leads the overall migration architecture, but you and the Data Engineering lead will drive the day-to-day prioritization and execution planning together.

s.h: What you get to do in this role
s.t:
Product Vision & Roadmap
Own the product vision and roadmap for FinOps data engineering (ELT pipelines, data lake, source onboarding) and platform services (Trino, Coder, Lightdash, Jupyter, Redash, Nessie).
Define what “production-ready” means for data pipelines and platform services. Establish SLAs for data freshness, pipeline reliability, and platform availability, and use them to steer prioritization.
Sequence the roadmap across both teams so that platform capabilities land ahead of the pipeline and analytics work that depends on them.
Gate roadmap phases on clear readiness criteria rather than arbitrary timelines. Ensure each phase builds on a proven foundation.
Data Engineering & Pipeline Product
Own requirements and prioritization for ELT pipeline development. Define which sources to onboard, in what order, and what the acceptance criteria are for each.
Specify the data contracts, quality expectations, and freshness SLAs for each pipeline, translating business needs into work the data engineering team can build and validate against.
Drive source onboarding to be fast and repeatable. Work with data engineers to templatize and automate the path from raw source to governed lakehouse table.
Translate data governance requirements (data classification, access control policies, lineage, retention) into concrete engineering specifications and acceptance criteria.
Ensure pipeline reliability is measurable and improving. Define the metrics, track them, and use them to prioritize investment in reliability over new features when needed.
Platform Services Product
Own requirements and prioritization for platform services alongside the platform services manager. Bring the user and stakeholder perspective; partner on feasibility and sequencing.
Define adoption and satisfaction targets for platform services. Understand how internal users experience Trino, Coder, Lightdash, and Jupyter, and drive improvements that reduce friction and increase self-service capability.
Advocate for developer experience improvements across the data engineering workflow. Identify pain points in how data engineers use workspaces, CI/CD, notebooks, and query tools, and work with the platform team to resolve them.
Drive platform service onboarding for new users and use cases, ensuring documentation, access provisioning, and initial support are smooth.
Stakeholder Management & Adoption
Serve as the primary intake point for requirements from FinOps practitioners, finance, capacity planning, and engineering teams that need data landed or platform capabilities extended.
Turn ambiguous asks into sequenced, shippable work with clear acceptance criteria. Push back on scope that doesn’t serve the roadmap, and negotiate timelines with stakeholders when needed.
Define the measurement model for success (pipeline SLA attainment, platform uptime, adoption breadth, source onboarding velocity, developer satisfaction) and report against it.
Communicate roadmap status, trade-offs, and dependencies to stakeholders in terms they can act on.
Migration & Cross-Team Alignment
Partner with the Data Engineering team on Cloudera-to-lakehouse migration planning, jointly owning wave sequencing, readiness criteria, and stakeholder communication for pipeline and platform workloads.
Coordinate with the Principal Engineer on overall migration architecture while driving the day-to-day prioritization and execution planning alongside Data Engineering leadership.
Align with the Analytics Engineering TPO (your peer) to ensure the data models and dashboards team has what it needs from the lake and platform layers.
Governance Translation
Translate enterprise data governance policies (from compliance, security, and data governance teams) into actionable specifications for the engineering teams.
Ensure data classification, access control, lineage tracking, and audit requirements are implemented in both the pipelines and the platform services.

Role Scope
Habitat Health is hiring its first Data Product Manager to report to the VP of Product. We are looking for a generalist, hands-on, highly technical individual contributor who will own the roadmap for Habitat's data products and infrastructure, setting direction and priorities across the data function. You will own data products end-to-end across the two major Habitat Health pillars that the data team supports:
Platform & Integrations , including Engineering / IT / Product / Technical & AI vendors
Dashboards & Reporting , across growth, clinical, financial, and administrative data sets
In this role you will serve as the key bridge between our Product and Data functions, working closely with C-Suite and VP level stakeholders to align on the right product strategy, then rolling up your sleeves and collaborating with our development team to build data products that align with business needs. To succeed as a Data PM, you will need to balance Habitat’s high level business objectives against end user needs and development constraints.
In a given week you'll move across all of the modes below: figuring out what's actually worth building (Discovery), writing specs precise enough for developers to build from without back-and-forth (Specs), running the Jira backlog and sprint process (Delivery), keeping development unblocked (Execution management), mocking up and shipping dashboards (Design, QC, UAT), and triaging the daily stream of ad hoc requests from a diverse set of data customers (Triage).

s.h: Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role
s.t:
Discovery : define the business problem before the build (e.g. is automating LOPMR for CMS audits the right priority this quarter?).
Build and ship : own the full delivery cycle – specs, Jira/sprint process, dashboard design and sign-off, UAT, and rollout.
Hands-on data work : use SQL and Git to independently query, validate, and review code, not just manage a backlog.
Triage : distinguish quick fixes from roadmap work across a steady stream of ad hoc requests.
AI fluency : use AI tools (e.g. Claude) to accelerate the work and model that fluency for the team.
Range : move across all Platform & Integrations, Clinical & Operational Services, Regulatory and Enterprise Reporting, helping shape how data product works at Habitat.

As a Customer Acceleration Product Adoption Manager, you will serve as the product owner for Okta’s suite of customer education offerings, while contributing to the broader Customer Acceleration post-sales portfolio, including success packages and related offerings.

You will bring product thinking and customer centricity to how we design, improve, and grow our education products, working cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, Customer Content, Field Sales, and Customer First to ensure our offerings meet customer needs and drive long-term adoption, retention, and growth.

Own the education subscription product roadmap: Serve as the product owner for Okta's education subscription, managing the backlog, defining requirements, and prioritizing improvements based on customer needs, business goals, and data insights. Develop a working knowledge of the public learning catalog and how it intersects with the subscription experience to inform roadmap decisions and ensure a seamless customer journey.

Define and measure impact: Establish success metrics for the education subscription and public catalog. Optimize the journey to expertise: Partner with the Platforms and Customer Content teams to identify friction points in the customer learning journey and advocate for improvements that make it easier for customers to find, access, and benefit from education resources at the right moment.
Connect education to the broader success journey: Partner with Customer Acceleration and Customer First leadership teams to contribute to the ongoing evolution of how education, success packages, and related offerings work together to deliver a cohesive, high-value customer experience.

About Allica Bank
Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.
Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.
Department Description
Allica Bank aims to provide Expert Banking for Business Britain by providing excellent customer experience and pioneering technology solutions to facilitate this.
The Autonomous Lending tribe runs across multiple business lines including Credit Operations and Underwriting, with a mission to build AI-first lending origination journeys, automating origination capabilities, data flows, and underwriting and operational workflow management.
The tribe is a critical driver for Allica to continue to realise its vision of providing a market leading relationship-based banking experience, at a speed and cost to serve the rest of the market cannot match.
Role Description
The Product Owner will lead the work to define, deliver and manage AI-enabled products across our lending journeys, bringing together product design and thinking with a strong working knowledge of what today’s AI can and cannot do.
You will be accountable for the roadmap of your team and for the full product lifecycle: discovery and design, day-to-day delivery, launch and adoption by colleagues and customers, and how risks are addressed once a product is live. You will aim to build robust, automated and well-governed systems and processes that enable us to move quickly and innovate our lending and financing products in the SME banking market.
Whilst a lot of the market aims to avoid the complex nature of SME businesses, we are going for it head on, designing simple and efficient solutions to the most complex problems in the market to provide excellent and efficient customer experience. We aim for our external view of the lending product, as well as our internal systems to be the best in market which will allow us to scale quickly to serve more UK SMEs, while doing so in a cost-effective manner.
Principal Accountabilities
Responsible for innovation and building end-to-end solutions for AI-enabled lending product, origination, underwriting and operational flows
Lead a small cross-functional team (e.g. a full stack engineer and AI specialist) to deliver your roadmap
Continuously review business needs, refine priorities and iterate towards measurable outcomes – judged on fewer requests for further information, more applications decided with AI, less colleague time per application across underwriting and credit operations, and risk outcomes no worse than the equivalent manual journey
Prototype and experiment quickly – vibe-code working prototypes yourself, close enough to the real thing that an engineer can harden it into production code
Determine the accuracy of AI solutions by analysing the data yourself and building the verified “ground truth” datasets that results are tested against, working with underwriters and credit operations colleagues to agree what a correct answer looks like
Take responsibility for launch and adoption – briefing stakeholders, training the teams who will use the product, and closing the loop on the feedback they give back
Produce the written work that keeps delivery moving and safe – clear descriptions of what we are building and why, a record of the important design decisions and trade-offs made, and the assessments needed to get a product approved and live, covering risk, security, cost, data and legal considerations, and taking the change through the bank’s governance and approval process
Line manage, coach and develop your team, setting a high bar for delivery and for the responsible use of AI
Personal Attributes & Experience
Knowledge of commercial lending origination and underwriting processes, principles and systems
Experience in a fast-moving or high-growth business
Proven track record of delivering agentic and data-driven products into live use
Strong process design, implementation and automation skills
Hands-on familiarity with Python, SQL and data analytics tools, alongside LLM tooling, prompt engineering and AI orchestration – you do not need to be an engineer or an analyst, but you should be able to build something that works, query the data yourself, and understand and sense-check what AI is producing
Understanding of privacy and safety considerations when applying LLMs in production, and of how to prove and monitor accuracy once a solution is live – ideally in a regulated environment
Strong analytical skills and business acumen, comfortable digging into data yourself to size a problem, measure performance and assemble the reference datasets accuracy is judged against
Metric and outcome driven approach – setting the measures up front, tracking them once a product is live, and stopping work that is not moving them
Experience working with or leading product and engineering teams, and comfortable in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the problem is as novel as the solution

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals.

You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Staff Product Manager for OpenTelemetry Experience, you’ll own the end-to-end journey for helping people and agents instrument workloads and successfully send useful OpenTelemetry data to Grafana Cloud.
Your mission is to make Grafana Cloud the easiest and most trusted destination for OpenTelemetry workloads. You’ll reduce the uncertainty, complexity, and failure points users encounter between deciding to adopt OpenTelemetry and receiving healthy, correctly attributed, and actionable telemetry in Grafana Cloud.
Teams can instrument workloads, directly or with the help of coding agents, through OpenTelemetry SDKs, automatic instrumentation technologies such as Beyla and SDK injection, or client-side OpenTelemetry Collectors. Each path presents different decisions, deployment requirements, configuration steps, and potential failure modes.

You’ll define a coherent experience that helps users choose the right approach, complete setup successfully, troubleshoot problems, and understand whether their telemetry is healthy and useful. You’ll design a future in which a growing share of instrumentation work is performed by coding agents acting on behalf of developers.

This means treating agents are first-class participants in the experience and ensuring that instrumentation options, configuration requirements, errors, and validation signals are structured, discoverable, and actionable by both humans and machines.

OpenTelemetry SDK onboarding and configuration
Automatic instrumentation experiences, including OBI/Beyla and SDK injection
Client-side OpenTelemetry Collector deployment and onboarding
Collector configuration, authentication, and initial connectivity
Guidance and machine-readable context that help people and agents choose the right instrumentation approach
Workflows that allow coding-agents to implement, configure and verify instrumentation safely
Troubleshooting missing, incomplete, malformed, or unhealthy telemetry
Validation signals that allow both people and agents to confirm that telemetry is healthy, correctly attributed, and usable in Grafana Cloud
The transition from receiving telemetry to activating the appropriate Grafana Cloud observability solution
Success does not stop when Grafana Cloud receives the first data point. Telemetry must arrive with the quality, context, and structure required to support meaningful observability outcomes. You’ll partner closely with teams responsible for experiences such as Application Observability, Kubernetes Monitoring, Infrastructure Observability, and Drilldown Apps to ensure OpenTelemetry workloads receive a first-class experience from initial setup through first value.
This is a horizontal Staff-level product leadership role spanning multiple products and engineering teams. You may not directly own every SDK, collector, instrumentation technology, or downstream application involved in the journey. You will, however, be accountable for the coherence of the overall customer experience, its success measures, and the cross-product strategy required to improve it.
AI will also be part of how you work, not only what you build. You’ll be expected to use AI tools regularly to accelerate customer-research synthesis, analyze product signals, explore technical workflows, prototype experiences, develop positioning content, and test agent-led instrumentation journeys. You’ll model thoughtful, hands-on adoption of AI while applying strong judgement to its outputs.
The role is not focused on developing OpenTelemetry as an open source project in isolation. You’ll engage with and contribute to the OpenTelemetry ecosystem where appropriate, while measuring success through customer activation and outcomes in Grafana Cloud.

Define the vision, strategy, and cross-product roadmap for the journey from an uninstrumented workload to healthy, useful telemetry in Grafana Cloud solutions
Create coherent, opinionated experiences that help users choose and implement the right approach across SDK instrumentation, automatic instrumentation, and Collector-based deployment while preserving the flexibility advanced users require
Identify and eliminate the leading causes of setup failure, abandonment, misconfiguration, and low-quality telemetry
Establish shared experience principles, priorities, and success criteria across the product and engineering teams contributing to the OpenTelemetry journey
Use customer research, product data, and market insight to prioritize investments and measure outcomes such as onboarding completion, time to useful telemetry, telemetry health, and workload expansion
Partner with downstream Grafana Cloud solution teams to create a coherent transition from telemetry ingestion to meaningful product activation

At Cloudflare, we are helping to build a better Internet, and part of that is making sure it’s easy to connect with anyone anywhere. We’re looking for a product manager who will help develop our Cloudflare Network Interconnect product line and make us easy to connect with while delivering unparalleled security and performance.
As a Product Manager for Cloudflare Network Interconnect, you will champion a mature, high-impact product that powers seamless, secure, and performant connectivity for organizations globally.

At Cloudflare, you'll join a mission-driven team dedicated to building a better Internet, with this role serving as the primary steward of our interconnect infrastructure's evolution and scale.

You will own the strategic direction, prioritizing features that enhance performance, driving roadmap decisions based on deep customer insights, and collaborating across engineering and cross-functional teams to deliver an exceptional user experience.

This is an opportunity to elevate a product that is already an industry staple, working in an environment where your decisions directly influence the stability and performance of the Internet itself.
As a member of a growing team of infrastructure product managers your responsibilities include:
Represent the customer, be it internal or external. Be the champion and voice of customers. Build intimate, personal customer relationships. Bring the customer's voice into the creation process.
Develop the product vision for your area. Ensure that your vision can work not just for your current set of customers, but for 10 or even 100 times your current set.
Evangelize the vision so that all stakeholders are aligned, have context and understand where we are going.
Make data-driven roadmap decisions. Make tough tactical prioritization decisions based off of data you collect, curate, and disseminate. Build trust with stakeholders by ensuring that your roadmap is understandable and sensible based on the data you present.
Measure success. Own the measures used to define success for your product. Success measures must be defined at the inception of a product and tracked throughout its lifecycle. Make measures visible to all stakeholders and interpret them into actionable conclusions and new hypotheses.
Author use cases and prioritize requirements. Translate observations and customer feedback into a prioritized product backlog. Author use cases based on specific real-world product applications and extrapolate detailed product requirements for the scenarios.
Collaborate across teams. We win or lose as a team. Product managers play a critical role in creating alignment between engineering teams and stakeholders. A collaborative attitude is essential to the job.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
Roblox’s 21-month Associate Product Manager (APM) rotational program is designed to cultivate well-rounded product leaders through mentorship, guided learning, and hands-on execution. Collaborate with cross-functional partners in design, data science, product marketing and engineering to write specifications, experimentation plans and go-to-market briefs.
Conduct user research, gather feedback, and analyze data to identify creator community needs and opportunities.
Support market research and competitive analysis to inform product decisions.
Upon completing the 21-month rotational cycle, APMs have the opportunity to graduate and join Roblox as a full time Product Manager (PM) within a specific team at Roblox.

A collaborative partner, comfortable sharing and presenting your ideas across different audiences.

About us Since 2000, ITA Logistics Group has been making shipping simpler, more transparent, and more efficient for businesses. With our platforms LetMeShip and ParcelParcel , companies can quickly compare and directly book their daily shipping needs. By bringing together a wide range of carriers on our platforms, we combine modern technology with personal service.
Across several locations in Europe, our teams work every day to simplify shipping processes in a sustainable way. We believe in open collaboration and fast decision-making. That’s why we are looking for people who take ownership, contribute ideas, and want to actively shape the future with us.
Your mission As our (Technical) Product Owner (m/f/d), you will be part of our Product Team and take ownership of key technical interfaces and integrations across our platforms. Your main focus will be on our Customer APIs, the Unified Carrier Interface (UCI), and, going forward, the Unified Financial Platform (UFP) as well as our HubSpot integration.
You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, and Business. You understand technical dependencies, translate different requirements into clear priorities, and work closely with our teams to ensure that our integrations are reliable and continuously evolving.
You will collaborate closely with our Product Owners, Technical Business Analyst, Software Engineers, and Data Insights team while also acting as an important point of contact for internal stakeholders, customers, carriers, and external partners.
Your Key Responsibilities You own and continuously develop the roadmap for our Customer APIs across LMS Enterprise and LMS Next.
You drive the migration of our API customers from LMS Enterprise to LMS Next, identifying and prioritizing the features and carrier integrations required to make the transition successful.
You act as a technical point of contact for our API customers, supporting them with questions, troubleshooting, and technical challenges.
You take ownership of the development of our Unified Carrier Interface (UCI) in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
You analyze requirements for carrier features and services, translate them into clear requirements for Engineering, and support QA in defining relevant test cases.
You communicate directly with our carriers to clarify technical requirements and integration specifics.
Once live, you take ownership of our Unified Financial Platform (UFP) and manage its backlog, requirements, and further development.
You continuously monitor our existing HubSpot integration and prioritize adjustments based on evolving business needs and feedback.
Across all these areas, you connect Engineering, business stakeholders, carriers, and external partners, ensuring clear requirements, priorities, and decisions.
What you need to succeed You have a technical background, for example in Software Engineering or Computer Science, or several years of experience working at the intersection of Product and Engineering.
You have experience as a Product Owner or Product Manager, ideally working with APIs, platforms, or technical integrations.
You have a solid understanding of APIs, API design, versioning, and migration strategies and feel confident engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineers.
You are able to understand complex technical topics and translate them clearly for different audiences.
You are confident in stakeholder management and know how to balance and prioritize competing technical and business needs.
You are comfortable managing multiple workstreams and adapting to changing priorities while keeping a clear overview of what matters most.
You enjoy working collaboratively across teams and locations, including with colleagues in Hamburg and Naarden.
You are curious about AI tools and digital solutions and enjoy exploring new ways to improve productivity, processes, and workflows.
Experience in logistics, parcel, or freight tech, particularly with carrier API integrations, is a plus.
Familiarity with HubSpot or CRM integrations, as well as financial or invoicing systems and interfaces, is also a plus.
Across all these areas, you connect Engineering, business stakeholders, carriers, and external partners, ensuring clear requirements, priorities, and decisions.
Why ITA Logistics Group? You can expect a work environment where new ideas are genuinely welcomed and feedback is not just accepted, but actively encouraged. We challenge the status quo, embrace agile ways of working, and continuously evolve. This also means making use of modern digital tools and AI-driven solutions that support your day-to-day work and help make processes more efficient.

At Swoop , our mission is simple: Improving patient outcomes. As a market leader in AI-driven, data-powered, and privacy-compliant healthcare engagement, we connect the signals that drive earlier diagnosis, better treatment decisions, and sustained adherence.
Our integrated, privacy-safe platform, enables life sciences companies to drive measurable patient and commercial outcomes with actionable intelligence — spanning patient and HCP audience targeting, community engagement, AI-powered web solutions, coordinated omnichannel activation, and prescription fulfillment.
We believe our people are our greatest asset. Swoop fosters a culture of innovation and continuous learning, providing employees with rich opportunities for professional growth. This commitment to our team earned us the "Best Places to Work" recognition from Business Intelligence Group in 2025 and 2026. We are driven by a patient-first philosophy and passionate about leveraging technology to create a healthier future.
After becoming an independent company in 2024, Swoop experienced significant growth and demonstrated an unwavering commitment to innovation, talent development, and enhancing the patient experience.

Our acquisition of MyHealthTeam in January 2025 and Nimble in May 2026 helped us further bridging the gap between healthcare brands and patients for more impactful and targeted engagement. Empowering millions of patients nationwide to connect, share resources, and access medically verified information to better manage their health.

MyHealthTeam hosts the largest and most engaged patient social networks in healthcare, offering more than 70 condition-specific communities for chronic and rare conditions.

As a prescription fulfillment and patient engagement platform, Nimble empowers independent and regional pharmacies to deliver a modern, consumer-friendly healthcare experience while streamlining pharmacy operations.
If you're a driven professional seeking to make a real difference in healthcare marketing at a fast-growing, innovative company, join Swoop and help us revolutionize how brands connect with patients and HCPs.

MyHealthTeam, a Swoop company, runs online communities to help people facing chronic conditions and rare diseases see around the next corner by bringing together medically sound information and the experience of real people. Patients find each other, ask the questions they can’t ask anywhere else, and get information they can act on.
That engagement is what makes our commercial solutions valuable to our partners: pharma and agency partners. They can reach real, condition-specific communities through sponsored content, patient education, awareness programs, and custom media experiences — creating revenue that keeps the communities free for patients.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to serve as the Product Team's dedicated lead for commercial solutions. You will wake up thinking about innovative solutions that get our pharma partners and agency clients excited about the unique ways they can engage with and educate patients and caregivers. The bar is that every solution both earns its place with patients and gives our partners something they can't get anywhere else.
You will partner with a best-in-class Business Development and Sales Solutions team to turn client and market signals into solutions worth building. They bring the client lens and lead packaging with sales and B2B marketing; you bring the product craft. Together you shape what we take to market.
As new solutions launch, you’ll collaborate directly with operational teams who bring them to life: Content & Editorial, Sales Ops, Acquisition and Product Marketing, and Alliance Management. You’ll stay close to the performance of in-market solutions to identify opportunities to iterate and improve.
You’ll join a Product Team of six and work closely with counterparts focused on user growth and engagement to find commercial opportunities in the core feature roadmap. You will work with a builder team rapidly transforming to an AI-driven product development lifecycle — from rapid prototyping in discovery to agentic coding in build.

Lead Zero to One Development for Community Commercial Solutions

Prototype concepts for client feedback to rapidly iterate toward market fit.

Skillfully translate concepts into clear product requirements and steer them gracefully through the product development lifecycle, from discovery to launch and continued improvement.

Who We Are
Cobalt was founded on the belief of a fundamental human aspiration: the desire to live better and safer. It all started in 2013, when our founders realized that pentesting can be better. Today our diverse, fully remote team is committed to helping organizations of all sizes with seamless, effective and collaborative Offensive Security Testing that empower organizations to OPERATE FEARLESSLY and INNOVATE SECURELY.
Our customers can start a pentest in as little as 24 hours and integrate with advanced development cycles thanks to the powerful combination of our SaaS platform coupled with an exclusive community of testers known as the Cobalt Core.

Accepting just 5% of applicants, the Cobalt Core boasts over 500 closely vetted and highly skilled testers who jointly conduct thousands of tests each year and are at the forefront of identifying and helping remediate risk across a dynamically changing attack surface.
Cobalt is an Equal Opportunity Employer and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive workforce at our company. At Cobalt we aspire to engage with diverse individuals, communities, and organizations in order to continue to nurture our unique rich diverse culture. Join our team, and be your true self to do your best work.
Description
All organizations need security testing for their software and we are building the world’s largest and smartest pentest management platform to help solve this challenge at scale.
As a Contract Senior Staff Product Manager , you will drive the definition, delivery, and adoption of new product features and ecosystem integrations. You will be responsible for taking the lead of our next gen deliverables, from user discovery and roadmap prioritization to go-to-market execution - ensuring that our platform evolves to solve the most pressing challenges in the security workflow.
This is a full-time contractor position providing hourly coverage from October through the end of February . In this role, you will merge attention to detail with the ability to understand and align business objectives, while working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to drive customer insights and inputs directly into the development process. You will work closely with our other Customer Experience and Pentester Experience teams.
What You Would Do
As a member of a growing team of product managers your responsibilities include:
Rapidly acquire new technical knowledge while maintaining meticulous attention to detail. Champion the strategic product direction across the organization, ensuring internal and external synchronization while serving as a subject matter expert on industry developments and defensive security operations.
Represent our customers. Work with Product Design, Product Marketing, Sales and Customer Success teams to bring the customer’s voice into the development process.
Manage the platform next-gent feature deliverables . Make tough tactical prioritization decisions while enabling the company to think long-term.
Collaborate across teams. We win or lose as a team. Product managers are a critical role in creating alignment between engineering teams and stakeholders.
Have familiarity with information security, security operations, vulnerability disclosure, vulnerability management and other security domain areas.
Become an expert in pentesting best practices. You are ready to discuss and demonstrate product details with developers, product designers, security operations, pentesters, customers and sales prospects.
Measure success. Own the measures used to define success for your product. Success measures must be defined at the inception of a product and tracked throughout its lifecycle. Make measures visible to all stakeholders and interpret them into actionable conclusions and new hypotheses.
Lead Go-to-Market (GTM) Readiness: Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to orchestrate successful feature launches. Develop launch strategies, create internal training materials, and support the creation of customer-facing collateral to ensure seamless adoption.
Maintain technical fluency in the operational workflows of modern cybersecurity tools, including vulnerability management or offensive security platforms. Evaluate how these tools function within a customer’s security environment to inform product development.

8+ years experience in Product Management and 3+ years experience in cybersecurity tools (vulnerability management or offensive security platforms), with a demonstrated ability to discover new opportunities and then define and deliver products. Experience in fast-growing software companies is a plus.
Strong technical skills - you can work alongside customers to help debug and improve our integration offerings.
Strong customer and stakeholder empathy. You must not only be the voice of the customer but at various times the voice of marketing, finance, engineering, sales and customer success. You must be able to channel many points of view.
Strong written and verbal communication skills. You’re great at explaining highly technical topics to technical and non-technical audiences, with a talent for building empathy for user problems.
Strong analytical capabilities is a plus.
Strong bias for action, creative thinking, innovation and data-driven product decision-making.
A can-do attitude and ability to juggle multiple priorities simultaneously.
Experience with agile software development.
Experience working with global team members (This team is a global team).
Hands-on experience with core cybersecurity tooling (e.g., DAST/SAST scanners, vulnerability management systems, or pentest workflow platforms). Articulate how security teams utilize these tools to identify, prioritize, and remediate risk, understanding the "why" behind the tooling workflow beyond simple API integrations.
Strong technical and product communication skills: Ability to translate complex security concepts into clear documentation, user guides, and release notes tailored to both technical developers and business stakeholders.
Full-time availability for the duration of the contract. You must be able to commit to full-time hourly coverage from October through the end of February, with no planned extended absences or vacations during the contract period (excluding recognized company holiday’s).

Traditional banking has never really given you control over your financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance . That means making financial services easy and accessible for over 6.5M users.
We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close. We follow the same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world.

If you own outcomes rather than tasks, stay close to what users need, and refuse to wait for someone else to fix what's broken — you'll find people here who work exactly in the same way. And together, you'll build something worth being proud of.
What you'll be doing
As our Product Manager - Payments, you'll take full ownership of Consumer Payments within the Features & Payment domain — spanning debit cards, SEPA Credit Transfers, QR payments, and more — building and scaling the products millions of people use every day. Here's what that looks like in practice:
Discover the Right Problems – Combine direct user evidence with product data, market signals and regulatory insight to frame and validate problems before and during delivery, not only at kick-off.
0→1 Product Leadership – Drive strategy and execution for new payment products and features, from first concept to launch.
Scaling What Works – Take live products beyond launch: grow adoption and activation, expand coverage and use cases, and harden reliability as volumes increase. Treat adoption, reliability, support demand and realised value as product outcomes, not launch metrics.
Consumer-Facing Experience – Own the UX and customer-facing side of payments, ensuring complex financial mechanics are intuitive, transparent and seamlessly integrated into Satispay.
Product Definition & Documentation – Write clear Product Requirements for Engineering and stakeholders, carrying the user's perspective into every decision.
Cross-functional Alignment – Act as a strategic orchestrator across Customer Care, Finance, Compliance, Marketing, Legal and FinCrime/Fraud to align priorities around a shared product vision — designing experiences that meet regulatory requirements such as PSD2, SCA and AML rather than working around them.
External Partnerships – Work alongside our scheme and delivery managers on relationships with card schemes, issuing processors and payment providers: shape the roadmap you depend on, hold partners to their commitments, and turn their capabilities into user value.
Data-Driven Optimisation – Analyse product usage and performance metrics to optimise payment features and uncover new market opportunities.
Process Evangelism & Mentorship – Advocate for thorough documentation and efficient workflows to help the team anticipate obstacles and ensure smooth product delivery.

This role needs someone who can hold both sides of payments: the consumer experience and the rails underneath it.
Product Experience – 3+ years as a Product Manager in payments, banking or fintech.
Launch & Scale Track Record – Proven experience shipping products from scratch and growing live products through their scaling phase.
Payments Fluency – Deep experience with at least one payment rail — card issuing, SEPA transfers or account-to-account — and enough familiarity with the mechanics behind them (authorisation and settlement, scheme flows, chargebacks and disputes) to hold a conversation with Engineering and providers alike.
Financial & Analytical Skills – Strong grasp of payment economics — interchange and scheme fees, provider costs, fraud losses — and the ability to build a business case and read performance data without waiting for BI.
Regulated-Environment Comfort – Ability to design great experiences within regulatory constraints (PSD2, SCA, AML) and to treat Compliance, Legal and Fraud as partners rather than gatekeepers.
Stakeholder Management – Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams (Engineering, UX, BI, Finance, Compliance).
Language Skills – Professional fluency in English. Italian isn't required — we work in English .
Don't worry if you don't tick every box. We believe in the power of different viewpoints and strengths. Your unique perspective is important as we build something special: if you're passionate and can make a difference, we truly encourage you to apply.

Do you know what product management is really about? If you do, then you know it isn't roadmaps, tickets or beautifully groomed backlogs. It's finding a real, expensive, unglamorous problem that people live with every day - and shipping something that makes it go away. That is product.
At Shape Construction, we are building software that transforms how construction projects are delivered. It's born out of real project experience and designed to bring clarity, structure and performance to complex environments.
The problem we are solving is one of the oldest in the industry: what actually happens on a construction site never makes it, intact, to the people who need it. Supervisors, field engineers and site managers see reality first: work blocked, plans deviated from, instructions given verbally, conditions nobody planned for.

That knowledge lives in heads, notebooks, camera rolls and group chats. Meanwhile the people responsible for the commercial health of the project are working weeks behind, from whatever fragments they can piece together. By the time anyone needs to prove what happened, the evidence has gone cold.
We are building the platform that closes that gap. Tools the site genuinely wants to use, capturing what happens as it happens, and then turning that raw signal into structured, trustworthy records that let commercial and project leadership make decisions, hold their ground and protect margin they would otherwise have written off.
This is your opportunity to own a core part of that. You won't be handed a roadmap to administer, you'll shape it, defend it, and be measured on whether customers are genuinely better off. If you like being close to messy real-world problems, have strong opinions about what to build and the discipline to kill your own ideas when the evidence says so, keep reading.

About Customer Portal
Customer Portal exists to make Veriff's product sell itself. The Portal serves two purposes. It allows our customers to operate Veriff products — setting up and configuring products, consulting verification session details, reporting issues.

And it is a privileged surface for customers to discover, try, buy and expand through a seamless self-serve experience, connecting product usage, onboarding and growth in one place. It unites forces with GTM to automate acquisition, upsell, cross-sell and retention, with end-to-end ownership of the customer persona. The area is evolving fast.

What began as a self-serve growth surface (Station) is becoming the customer-facing window into Veriff's accuracy and fraud advantage for our largest enterprise customers.
The shape of this role
This is an IC-first leadership role, and the first genuine step into product leadership — distinct from a strong senior IC. At first you will lead through craft, authority and influence. You own the strategy, discovery, roadmap and delivery for your product area.
As you refine the strategic themes for this large product, we expect you to propose the team configuration needed to support our growth and company objectives. That will move you progressively from IC to manager, while retaining hands-on ownership of at least one part of the Customer Portal area in the mid-term. We will deliberately assess for both the IC craft bar and the latent management capability, because the role is designed to traverse the line.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the Customer Portal area, tied explicitly to Veriff's commercial model and revenue drivers.
Run disciplined, continuous discovery with customers, and translate it into well-defined problem statements and a sequenced roadmap.
Make transparent prioritisation and trade-off calls across product ambition, technical sustainability and business urgency — especially where capability gaps mean we cannot do everything at once.
Define success metrics before building, and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not output.
Partner as a credible peer to Engineering, GTM, Fraud Ops and Design. Be the connective tissue that turns internal expertise into a customer-facing product.
Own launch as a discipline from the start — internal platform releases and external GTM — not a milestone at the end.
Set and uphold the product-craft bar. Mentor PMs and, in time, build and lead the team.
Champion AI internally, implementing new best practices for faster product discovery and delivery.

You are a product leader who has earned authority through the quality of your thinking rather than a title.
You have owned a product area end-to-end
From strategy through discovery, delivery and launch. You are equally comfortable in the messy front end of a problem and in the discipline of shipping.
You are looking for the step where your impact starts to come through others, and you are excited that this role begins as an individual leader and grows into managing a team — not the other way around.
You think commercially
You instinctively connect what you build to how the business grows, and you explain the “why” behind a product bet in terms of revenue, retention and customer trust, not just features and flows.
You run discovery as a continuous discipline
You get close to customers, including demanding enterprise accounts, and you can tell the difference between what they ask for and what they actually need.
You turn that into sharp problem statements and a phased roadmap where every step delivers a real customer outcome.
You prioritise ruthlessly and transparently
When there are more good ideas than capacity, you make the hard calls about what not to do, and you can articulate the reasoning.
You define success before you build. When something goes wrong, you own it without deflection and change how you work as a result.
You lead through influence, not authority
You build credibility with engineering, go-to-market, design and operations partners as a genuine peer, and you reach good decisions with people who do not report to you.
You stay calm under uncertainty, create space for views that differ from your own, and commit gracefully once a call is made.
You raise the people around you
You set a high craft bar through your own work, share your thinking generously and give specific, useful feedback.
You are motivated by building and leading a team over time, with a realistic understanding that management is a different job — one focused on developing people and multiplying impact, not doing all the work yourself.
You stay current on your craft
You take pride in tracking how product management is evolving, and you consistently find time to experiment and fold what works into your practice.

Set a new pulse for healthcare!
We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to join the Patient Profile team in the Patient domain.
Your mission will be to make the patient health record complete, accurate and current enough that everything else we build can act on it, the health recommendations, care plans and assistant experiences that help people take their health into their own hands. You will work in a feature team developing the Patient Health Record, health trackers, patient account and online identity, contributing directly to the quality of the medical support we provide to both patients and practitioners.
A patient record is built from four channels: what patients enter themselves, what they share when preparing a consultation, what we retrieve from health professionals' systems, and what they connect from third-party sources such as Apple Health, Google Health Connect and national health record services.

Three of those channels belong to teams you will not manage. You will own the outcome across all four, the most leveraged place to sit in a health platform, and only reachable through other people.
You will also work inside a hard regulatory perimeter: health data, GDPR, consent by design.

s.h: Your responsibilities include but are not limited to
s.t:
Own the end-to-end patient data collection programme across every channel a patient record is built from, and be accountable for the result across all four
Define what a useful record actually means for the teams that depend on it, make that definition measurable, and instrument it rather than inheriting a dashboard
Partner with the channel-owning teams inside and outside the group: set the inter-team contracts, agree how each channel contributes, and arbitrate collection priorities
Own record quality and freshness rather than volume, alongside health data storage consent, patient account and online identity
Ship the layers that serve this data to the rest of the product: the patient feature store, the patient context service and the Patient Health Record feature
Lead the Patient Profile team's roadmap and delivery, from PHR (patient health record) and trackers through to the feature store and context service
Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you
s.t:
You have owned a coverage, completeness or data quality metric as your primary objective, and can say what it went from, to what, and over how long
You have worked at millions-of-records scale
You have moved that metric through teams that did not report to you, setting interfaces, contracts and SLAs with partner teams
You have shipped under a hard regulatory or consent constraint, in health, finance or identity, with privacy and consent by design
You have real technical depth: you have owned a data platform component as a product, a feature store, a context or profile service, or an identity layer.
You are fluent in English

s.h: It would be fantastic if you
s.t:
You have had a data quality problem surface only once it reached a downstream consumer, and you changed how you worked because of it
You have built a completeness or quality definition and made an organisation adopt it
You have worked on interoperability, health data standards, or identity and account models

As our first dedicated Product Manager, you'll take ownership of PartsOS, from discovery through delivery — alongside the founder who's been driving product so far. Based in Berlin, with occasional trips to see customers on site, you'll turn one of industry's most overlooked problems into software factories trust every day. You'll own everything from the customer conversation to the shipped solution, and grow with the product as we scale.
What You’ll Be Working On
Own product outcomes from discovery through delivery: talk to customers, frame the real problem, decide what we build, and ship it to production.
Shape the solution end to end, from the customer problem to the interface people actually use, making a complex domain feel simple.
Get hands-on with the data and the planning logic: query it yourself, understand how our forecasting and optimization models behave, and troubleshoot when something's off.
Put AI to work on real customer problems. Weave it deep into how spare-parts planning gets done as a core part of the product, not a bolt-on.
Stay close to our customers, from a world-famous motorsport team to global leaders in industrial automation and packaging, and turn what you learn into roadmap and measurable impact.

Must-Have
3+ years in product management for B2B, enterprise, or technical/data-heavy products, owning outcomes from discovery to delivery.
Comfortable getting hands-on with data: querying it yourself, understanding how optimization and forecasting models work, and troubleshooting rather than treating the system as a black box.
Genuinely fluent with AI: you know how to weave it into solving real customer problems, not just how to chat with it.
A talent for simplification: you turn complex, technical concepts into clear, usable product and can shape that experience yourself.
A self-starter with customers and ambiguity: you seek out users firsthand and are energized by being the first dedicated PM rather than following a finished playbook.
Fluent in English.
Great If You Also Bring
Strong working German: a real plus for getting close to our customers.
Exposure to ERP, supply chain, manufacturing, or other complex industrial domains.
Experience in a startup or high-growth environment.
Mindset
You want real ownership, from the customer problem to what ships in production.
You love the speed and access of working directly with a founder, and you want to learn at that pace.
You'd rather build something that ships than polish a finished product from a distance.
You're not squeamish about a bit of logic and math.
You prefer working in person over coordinating from a distance.
Not Quite Your Thing?
You want a tightly scoped backlog handed to you rather than owning the discovery yourself.
You prefer to stay above the technical detail and treat the optimization as a black box.
You need a fully remote setup.
You'd rather work in a large product org with clearly defined swim lanes than be the first PM in a fast-moving team.
A bit of math and data querying doesn't sound appealing.

Work shoulder to shoulder with a founder. This is about as close to the action as product gets: fast decisions, no bureaucracy, and the experience of building something real next to the person who started it. You'll learn an enormous amount, fast.
An office-first culture in Berlin. We believe the best work happens shoulder to shoulder. You'll join a team that values in-person collaboration, fast feedback loops, and the energy of working side by side every day. The occasional home office day is fine but if you're looking for a remote-heavy setup, this isn't the right role.
Annual team week. Once a year we all come together somewhere inspiring, working, building, and enjoying each other's company.
Shared success. You'll be part of our Virtual Stock Incentive Plan (VSIP), giving you a real stake in what we're building together.
A career that grows as fast as we do. In a wide-open category and a company moving this quickly, the ceiling is high. The scope and ownership you take on can grow as fast as the company does.
The Tools You’ll Be Using

Notion for knowledge, planning, and documentation
Teamwork to manage projects and priorities
HubSpot for CRM, pipeline insights, and commercial reporting
Excel for KPIs, modelling, and analysis
Outlook & Teams for email and scheduling
Slack for day-to-day communication and quick collaboration
Modern AI tools that we use throughout the business and which you'll help us push further
Ready to Be Part of Something Big?
You're at home in a customer conversation, a dataset, an AI workflow, and the guts of how the model behaves, and you're not squeamish about a little math. You want real ownership and love the speed of working directly with a founder. You'd rather build something that ships than polish a finished product from a distance.
